activated K‐ ras contributes to changes in cell surface expression of integrin subunits in human colon carcinoma.

the role of the K‐ras proto‐oncogene for regulation of cell surface expression of integrin receptors in colon carcinoma cells.
the role of the K‐ras oncogene in the regulation of integrin subunits in human colon carcinoma cell lines.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
activated K‐ ras in human colon carcinoma is involved in regulation, i.e. repression and induction, of integrin expression.
the K‐ras oncogene is a key player in the regulation of integrin subunits expression in human colon cancer cells.
activated K‐ ras in human colon carcinoma contributes to changes in expression of several integrins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
K‐ras is an important regulator of cell adhesion, and that K‐ras‐mediated alterations of integrin expression might contribute to tumor formation and progression.
activated K‐ ras is involved in the regulation of integrin gene expression and thereby in the regulation of the adhesiveness of colon carcinoma cells.

activated K‐ ras contributes to the malignant phenotype of colon carcinoma cells by downregulating the collagen/laminin‐receptor α1β1 and the fibronectin‐receptor β5, which are important for maintaining a nontransformed phenotype, and by upregulating the vitronectin‐ and laminin/collagene‐receptor α3β1, which are important in metastatic behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
activated K‐ ras is involved in the regulation of cell surface expression of several integrin subunits.
K‐ras is a key player in controlling expression of several integrin subunits.
